classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied bar models to group fractional parts into wholes or count denominator-sized parts in whole bars, then complete the indicated fraction form.

content.prompt: Convert these fractions. Use the bar models to help you.

spec.description: Three stacked bars divided into fifths; two full bars and two cells of the last bar are shaded.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied bar model is visible; the numerical response is hidden.

answer.worked:
Group the shaded fifths into wholes. There are 2 whole bars and 2 fifths left over.
$$\frac{12}{5}=2\frac{2}{5}$$

spec.description: Two stacked bars divided into sevenths; one full bar and five cells of the second bar are shaded.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied bar model is visible; the numerical response is hidden.

answer.worked:
Group the shaded sevenths into wholes. There is 1 whole bar and 5 sevenths left over.
$$\frac{12}{7}=1\frac{5}{7}$$

spec.description: Four stacked bars divided into sixths; three full bars and five cells of the fourth bar are shaded.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied bar model is visible; the numerical response is hidden.

answer.worked:
Group the shaded sixths into wholes. There are 3 whole bars and 5 sixths left over.
$$\frac{23}{6}=3\frac{5}{6}$$

spec.description: A fully shaded undivided bar above a bar divided into eighths with its leftmost cell shaded.
spec.mathematics: One whole can be split into 8 eighths; the additional shaded eighth makes 9 eighths.
spec.answerVisibility: The whole bar remains undivided as supplied. No numerical answer is printed.

answer.worked:
Split the whole bar into 8 equal parts. Count the 8 eighths and the additional shaded eighth: 9 eighths altogether.
$$1\frac{1}{8}=\frac{9}{8}$$

spec.description: Three fully shaded undivided bars above a bar divided into thirds with its leftmost two cells shaded.
spec.mathematics: Three wholes can be split into 9 thirds; the additional 2 thirds make 11 thirds.
spec.answerVisibility: The three whole bars remain undivided as supplied. No numerical answer is printed.

answer.worked:
Split each whole bar into 3 equal parts. The 3 wholes give 9 thirds. With the additional 2 shaded thirds, there are 11 thirds altogether.
$$3\frac{2}{3}=\frac{11}{3}$$
